⏰ Daily Schedule 🧹 How to Clean 📦 Restocking List

Kitchen

🟢 Green Cloths

🟢Kitchen only
Counters, appliances, sink, oil tray
Every day: use one clean Green cloth.
Wash the used cloth daily, so a clean set is always ready. Never use a Green cloth in the bathroom or bedrooms.
Daily every day

Tidy the counters

  1. Clear anything that doesn't belong on the counter, put it away first

Wash & put away dishes

Use dish soap. Wash dishes right after you use them. Do not let dirty dishes sit in the sink.

Wipe counters

  1. Spray the counter
  2. Wipe with the Green cloth
Dettol Antibacterial Surface Cleanser (Lime)Same bottle as the bathroom sink

Wipe the oil & condiment tray

  1. Wipe the outside of each bottle and jar. Oil drips down the sides and gets sticky
  2. Straighten the tray and put the lids back on. Make sure nothing sticky is left on the wood or the counter under the tray

Clean the glass stovetop

Only clean once fully cool
  1. Spray Kaneyo IH Kitchen Cleaner directly onto the cooled glass top
  2. Let the spray sit for a short time before wiping. It loosens oil, splatters, and burnt stains so they wipe away easily
  3. Wipe clean with a soft cloth
Note: this bottle can also be used on the kitchen wall and the outside of the range hood, not just the stovetop. Check the back of the bottle. It may say how long to let the spray sit before wiping. If this bottle is empty, use one of these instead: Jif Cream with micro crystals, or a paste of baking soda and water left on for 20 minutes, or a light spray of vinegar and water for small daily marks.
Never use these on this glass top: steel wool, rough scrub pads or powders, bleach, ammonia, or rust remover. These will scratch and stain the glass forever. This is what caused the stains already on the glass.
Kaneyo IH Induction & Gas Stove Glass Cleaner (400g)Homey Bear, HKTVmall, confirmed owned

Clean the sink

  1. Spray, wipe with the Green cloth, rinse
Dettol Antibacterial Surface Cleanser, or dish soapEither works

Empty bins

  1. Take out the old garbage bag, wipe the inside, put in a new garbage bag

Sweep and mop floor: always last

  1. Sweep first, all loose dirt off the floor
  2. Fill the mop bucket about halfway with warm water (roughly 4 liters), add 1 tablespoon of dish soap, stir
  3. Dip the mop, squeeze it out well, damp not dripping
  4. Work backward toward the door. This way, you never step on the clean floor
  5. Let air dry
SWIPE 紅威寶 Super Concentrate Dishwashing DetergentNo dedicated floor cleaner needed, same as every room

Rice cooker: wash pot, lid & steam vent

  1. Remove the inner cooking pot, the inner lid, and the steam vent cap
  2. Wash all three in warm water with a drop of dish soap. Do this every time the rice cooker is used, not just once a day
  3. Dry them completely before putting them back together
  4. Wipe the outer body with a damp cloth. Check the heating plate inside the base for stuck rice grains and wipe those away too
Dish soap + warm waterManufacturer-confirmed method (Zojirushi)
Caring for Your Zojirushi Rice Cooker (official)
Scan with phone camera to watch

Toaster oven: crumb tray & inside

  1. Unplug first, and let it cool completely
  2. Slide out the crumb tray and rack. Wash them with a sponge and mild dish soap. Rinse and dry them
  3. Wipe the inside walls and glass door with a soapy sponge. For the door glass, you can also spray glass cleaner onto a cloth first, then wipe the glass with the cloth
Note: never put the toaster oven itself in water. Only wash the tray and rack that come out.
Mild dish soapOptional: glass cleaner for the door only
How to Clean a Toaster Oven (Howcast)
Scan with phone camera to watch

Tea/coffee maker: daily wipe-down

  1. Wipe the outside and the buttons with a damp cloth
  2. Wash the glass carafe with dish soap after each use. Rinse and dry it
Note: this machine's exact brand couldn't be identified from the photo (Chinese-labeled preset buttons), so the internal descaling steps aren't confirmed yet. Hard water buildup in the water lines is common in Hong Kong and usually needs an occasional descale, but the right method depends on the model. A photo of the brand label/nameplate (often on the back or base) would let this be looked up properly instead of guessed.

Blender: self-clean rinse

  1. Fill the container about halfway with warm water. Add 2 to 3 drops of dish soap
  2. Put the lid on tightly. Turn the blender to a high speed for 10 to 15 seconds
  3. Empty the container and rinse it under the tap
Note: do not put the container or lid in the dishwasher. Wash them by hand, or use the self-clean rinse method above.
Dish soap + warm waterManufacturer-confirmed method (Vitamix)
Vitamix Self-Cleaning Container Demonstration (official)
Scan with phone camera to watch

Water dispenser: spout & drip tray

  1. Switch off and unplug before cleaning
  2. Remove the drip tray. Wash it with soapy water. Rinse it, then let it air-dry
  3. Wipe the spout and outer panel with a damp cloth
Note: never use rough scrub pads, strong chemicals, or rough scrubbers on this water dispenser (from the Philips manual). Watch for the Descale light on the panel. When it turns on, press and hold the button for 3 seconds to start the descale cycle. This light turns on based on how much the dispenser has been used, not on a fixed date.
Soapy water, soft cloth onlyOfficial Philips manual

Microwave: inside & outside

  1. Wipe outside and inside with a damp cloth, mild dish soap if needed
  2. Wash the glass turntable and roller ring in warm soapy water
Note: for stuck-on splatters, heat 1 cup of water with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice or vinegar for 2 to 5 minutes. Let it sit for 1 minute before wiping. The steam makes the dirt easier to wipe away (from Panasonic support). Never use harsh cleaners or rough scrubbers inside the microwave.
Mild dish soap, or water + lemon/vinegar steamManufacturer-confirmed (Panasonic)
Panasonic Microwave Oven: Care and Cleaning (official)

Wipe the outside of the fridge

  1. Wipe the door and handle with a damp cloth. Stainless steel shows fingerprints fast
  2. Dry with a second cloth so there are no streaks

Review the fridge for leftovers

  1. Check every container every day, not just when the fridge looks full. This includes the dog's cooked food, not only our own food
  2. Throw away anything cooked more than 3 to 4 days ago and still sitting in the fridge. Bacteria can grow even if the food still looks, smells, and tastes fine
  3. Move older items to the front. This way, you see them first and use them first
  4. Check the pantry and fridge. Use the "Always Keep Stocked" list below. If something is low, write it on the fridge notepad. That is all you need to do
Note: keep the fridge at 4°C (40°F) or below. Put cooked food (ours or the dog's) in the fridge within 2 hours of cooking it (1 hour if the kitchen is hot).
Note on the dog's food: it is cooked once a week, one batch for all 7 days. Only keep 3 to 4 days' worth in the fridge at a time (labeled, top shelf). Put the rest in small sealed containers in the freezer right after cooking. Move one container from the freezer to the fridge to thaw before it is needed, then the same 3-to-4-day fridge rule applies once it is thawed.
You do not need to order anything yourself. If something is low or finished, write it on the fridge notepad. Faith will order it online.

Where everything goes: your fridge has 4 shelves and 2 drawers in the main part, plus a left door and a right door with 7 shelves between them. The dog's food is labeled and cooked, so it goes on the top shelf with our own leftovers. The same food safety rules apply to the dog's food too.

Main Compartment
Shelf 1 (Top)
Leftovers, Ready-to-Eat & Dog Food
Cooked meals, deli meats, drinks you will finish soon, and the dog's cooked food (labeled, only 3 to 4 days' worth at a time, the rest stays frozen). The most stable shelf, safely above raw food. Write the date cooked on the label. Check it every day. Throw it away after 3 to 4 days.
Shelf 2
Dairy
Milk, yogurt, cheese, sour cream. This part of the fridge stays a steady temperature, which keeps these foods safe.
Shelf 3
Eggs & Prepped Ingredients
Egg carton (keep it in its original box, do not move it to the door), sauces you are using, and chopped vegetables for tonight's meal.
Shelf 4 (Bottom)
Raw Meat, Poultry & Fish
Always keep raw meat in a sealed container or tray. This is the coldest shelf in the main part of the fridge, so drips from raw meat cannot fall onto food on other shelves.
Two pull-out drawers, below the bottom shelf
Vegetables
Carrots, leafy greens, herbs. This drawer keeps more moisture in the air, if yours has a setting for that.
Fruit
Apples, berries, anything that goes bad quickly in a moist drawer.
Door (2 Panels)
Left Door
Shelf 1
Small Jars / Spare Room
Whatever's small enough to fit.
Shelf 2
Jams, Pickles & Spreads
Jam, pickles, mayo, and other jarred spreads.
Shelf 3
Water Pitcher & Drinks
The water filter pitcher, sparkling water, and water bottles.
Shelf 4 (The Big One)
Condiments
Ketchup, mustard, soy sauce, chili sauce, salad dressing. Every squeeze bottle and sauce jar goes here. This shelf is meant to be the fullest one.
Right Door
Shelf 1
Bread & Bagged Items
Bread or other bagged items that need the fridge.
Shelf 2
Jars & Pickled Items
More jars and bottles, including pickled vegetables. If you are not sure where something goes, put it here, not in the left door.
Shelf 3
Deli Container & Cold Bag
A sealed deli container or leftover container, and a cold bag.
This right door list comes from a photo. Tell Faith if anything here needs to change.
Never store milk or eggs in the door, either side. The temperature in the door changes too much.

🛒 Always Keep Stocked

This is a starting list. Faith is still checking and changing it. If something is not on this list, but you notice it is always running low, write it on the fridge notepad anyway.

In the fridge
  • Eggs
  • Milk
  • Butter
  • Cheese
  • Ham / deli meat
  • Yogurt
  • Garlic & onions
  • Fresh vegetables (carrots, leafy greens)
  • Fresh fruit
In the pantry
  • Rice
  • Cooking oil
  • Pasta / noodles
  • Bread
  • Coffee / tea
  • Dog food ingredients

Put all products away

Put every bottle, spray, and cloth back in its place. Do not leave anything out on the counter.

Weekly once a week

Deep-clean the fridge

  1. Take everything out of the main part, the drawers, and the door bins. This includes the dog's food container
  2. Wipe every shelf, drawer, and door bin with the Dettol spray. Dry them
  3. Wipe the rubber seal on the door too. Crumbs and spills hide there
  4. Check the date on every item while it is all out on the counter. This is the easiest time to find anything that has gone bad
  5. Put everything back in the same place, using the fridge map above
Once In A While rotate through these

Clean the range hood filter

  1. Remove the metal mesh grease filter (it slides or clips out)
  2. Wash it by hand in warm soapy water with a soft sponge. Or wash it in the dishwasher on a low-temperature setting
  3. Wipe the outside of the range hood with a soft damp cloth and mild detergent. Do not use rough scrubbers or strong chemicals. The Kaneyo IH Kitchen Cleaner (the one used on the stovetop) can also be used on the outside of the range hood and exhaust fan
Note: clean this at least once a month. Clean it more often if you cook a lot, or if you cook oily food often (from Smeg's official guide).
How to Clean Your Hood or Extractor Fan (Smeg official)
Scan with phone camera to watch

Deep-clean the rice cooker

  1. Wipe off any stuck rice or dirt from the edges of the lid and the inside of the outer body. Use a damp cloth or paper towel

Descale the water dispenser

  1. Do this only when the Descale light on the panel turns on. It does not happen on a fixed schedule
  2. Press and hold the Descale button for 3 seconds to start the cycle. Then follow the instructions shown on the panel
